title: Restriction and extension by zero for modules on a localized site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a Grothendieck site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $U$ be an object, and let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Give $\mathcal C/U$ the localized topology and write $\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal C)$ and $\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal O|_U}(\mathcal C/U)$ for the categories of sheaves of modules [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $j_U^*:\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal O|_U}(\mathcal C/U)$ be restriction, $G\mapsto G|_U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and for a sheaf $F$ of $\mathcal O|_U$-modules let $j_{U!}F=P_F^\#$ be the sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of its extension-by-zero presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $P_F$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf], functorial in $F$ (the *extension by zero*). Then $j_U^*$ is an exact functor, and $j_{U!}$ is an exact functor left adjoint to it: $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(j_{U!}F,G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O|_U}(F,j_U^*G)$ naturally in the $\mathcal O|_U$-module $F$ and the $\mathcal O$-module $G$.

proof.text: Retain the actual module restriction overFunctor and the actual direct-sum extension presheaf followed by module sheafification. Construct the presheaf Hom equivalence explicitly: restrict a map to each DirectSum.lof summand, and in the inverse direction apply DirectSum.toModule to the slice components. The restriction formula gives naturality; DirectSum.toModule.unique and DirectSum.toModule_lof give the inverse laws. Compose with PresheafOfModules.sheafificationHomEquiv and use Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv. Its unit is definitionally the prescribed summand injection followed by the sheafification unit. Adjunction.ext proves uniqueness from equality of units, checked on every section.

source.place: Section 03DH and Lemma 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero and exactness), with the same construction in sheaves of modules

proof.text: Restriction is additive by its sectionwise formula. The adjunction makes extension additive and colimit preserving (Mathlib Adjunction.left_adjoint_additive and leftAdjoint_preservesColimits). A monomorphism of module sheaves is injective at every evaluation; DirectSum.lmap_injective shows the extension presheaf preserves monomorphisms. Left exact module sheafification also preserves monomorphisms. Hence the sheafified extension is additive, preserves cokernels and monomorphisms, and is exact by Functor.preservesHomology_of_preservesMonos_and_cokernels. Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesHomology gives finite limits; the adjunction already gives finite colimits. This is the direct module argument of Stacks 03DJ, avoiding transport to the abelian extension.

proof.text: Supply abelian sheafification and its locally bijective equivalence criterion on the slice by transporting from equivSmallModel in universe max c v r, using the existing proved hasSheafify_coefficientUniverse and wEqualsLocallyBijective_coefficientUniverse helpers (whose proofs use Mathlib hasSheafifyEssentiallySmallSite and WEqualsLocallyBijective.ofEssentiallySmall). The forgetful functor Over.forget U is continuous and cocontinuous. Its sheafAdjunctionCocontinuous makes abelian restriction colimit preserving, and its sectionwise description preserves limits. Module restriction commutes definitionally with forgetting to abelian sheaves. Map each short exact complex through the exact module forgetful functor of [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], then through abelian restriction, and reflect short exactness through the faithful exact forgetful functor on the slice. The Mathlib finite-limit and finite-colimit criteria for additive functors between abelian categories prove the remaining two preservation clauses. All site and coefficient universes remain independent.
